target: S2 and D2: pooling answers about the same object/quantity across scene-family clips, multi-reference scale
base: submissions/trackA_probe5_families_merged.csv (only S2 or only D2 rows differ in each variant)
findings: 2D answers inside families are already consistent with the stated facts: leave-one-fact-out over 16-17 D2 stated facts scores .994 raw and .988 pooled (one bike speed moves from 4.6% to 5.2% error, across the 5% threshold); S2 has 3 checkable facts (.733; the only miss, simulation_0041 boat length 13.0 vs 10, is already set by T in probe 5).

Multi-reference scale in 2D: only 4 clips have >=2 family facts; leave-one-out .90 -> .95, all from simulation_0041 (overhead view, k=0.76 from boat length and speed, already handled by T/SIB in probe 5). Per-clip scale across cameras does not exist in 2D: deviations of a clip's answers from the other cameras correlate only 0.30 within a clip and K leaves the mean |log deviation| at 0.068. Within one camera view the per-clip scale is clearer (corr 0.51) but the gain is tiny (pseudo .956 -> .960). Not built.

Scene-family 'bases' are often the same camera: 0214/0215/0217 (top view of the cat room), 0236/0238/0240 and 0237/0239/0241 (horse scene), 0068-0075 (8 clips of the intersection share one camera), 0098-0103, 0257-0260. Counting clips as votes is wrong (TV-stand width: two clips of one camera say 0.44 m, the third 1.57 m). Votes are therefore camera views: clips whose high-pass edge maps correlate >= 0.6 (lighting-robust; thumbnail NCC fails on 0214 vs 0217) or identical renders, segmented twins joined to their original.

Cross-camera spread is real: in groups of the same object+quantity across cameras, 41% of D2 rows differ by >5% from the other clips' median (median |log| 0.034). Holding out each 2D camera in turn as the reference, pooling the other cameras (trimmed mean of log votes within 0.15 of the median; 2 votes: geometric mean when within 0.25; <=3 votes spread >0.35 left alone) gains +0.018 per changed D2 row (size +0.016, speed +0.021, displacement +0.028); pseudo MRA .894 -> .906. A synthetic check with heavy-tailed errors fitted to the observed pairwise spreads gives pseudo gain ~= real gain when errors are independent across cameras. With clip (not camera) votes the size gain was only +0.001..+0.008.

3D family clips' probe-5 answers as extra votes: +0.0177 per changed 2D row on more rows; a lone 2D camera pooled with 3D votes gains +0.0125..+0.025 (pseudo). But the one known S2 row it touches gets worse (simulation_0163 bowling pin 0.315 -> 0.351, truth 0.320; S3 votes are Claude's direct answers), so S2 keeps 2D votes only.

Wide disagreements are definition / occlusion differences, not noise, and are skipped by the guard: deer = antelope in 0243-0247 (the segmented twins rename it) measured 2.2 m by some cameras and 3.5-3.7 m by others (horns/tail); floor mirror width top view 0.78-0.86 vs side 0.55; house width 7.6-13.2. Distances between objects are excluded: identical prior text can hide different start configurations (0085/0086/0087: same car acceleration and bike speed, car-bike distance 4.9 vs 15.3 m).

Known val-on-test rows give almost no signal for 2D families: S2 has 13 family rows (0163, 0171: different astronaut motions per clip, correctly not pooled), D2 has 4 (0098_seg, a single camera). Known S2/D2 MRA unchanged by the 2D-vote variants (.7731/.9227).
D2 stated-fact transfer (T, 20 rows, not in probe 5): 19 are already within 5% of the stated value; only qid 109 (bike speed 4.77 vs stated 5.07) moves a threshold (+0.1 item).

Conclusion: family pooling is a small lever in 2D (expected D2 about +0.004..+0.005, S2 ~0). The large D3 gain came from per-clip scale errors in Claude's direct 3D answers; 2D geometry answers do not carry such errors, and most 2D family groups are single camera views.

Not built, possible D2 lever outside families: speed questions of an object whose acceleration is the stated prior can violate v(t) = v0 + a t (simulation_0198 droplet speed at 0.2 s = 0.98 by geometry while a = 9.7 m/s^2 gives ~1.94; direct answers 1.89-1.96).
